knowledge_point.title: Identifying an Invertible Function From Its Graph

question.:question/problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186124472/assets/a52725c3416d024c8bf73e72b96754df2912e6ef9428bce05b6732b0be5c8e51.png)

Which of the graphs above correspond to an invertible function?

Each graph shows its entire domain; an open circle excludes its endpoint.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A function is invertible if and only if it's a one-to-one function. To determine which of the functions are one-to-one, we use the horizontal line test.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186124472/assets/586598a86b36551723c64a87460e5a6668d13221210084f3aa5c785de726046d.png)

From the above, we see that:

- For graph III, any horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line. Therefore, this graph shows a one-to-one function. As a result, this function is invertible.

- For graphs I, II, IV, some horizontal lines intersect the curve more than once. These are not one-to-one functions. As a result, they are not invertible.

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only".

Which of the graphs above correspond to an invertible function?

Each graph shows its entire domain; an open circle excludes its endpoint.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A function is invertible if and only if it's a one-to-one function. To determine which of the functions are one-to-one, we use the horizontal line test.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186124472/assets/a33b51d5e7cfbf4be81588f640b90187eaa42c4b53ff3f33eb9a7292caefebd4.png)

From the above, we see that:

- For graph IV, any horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line. Therefore, this graph shows a one-to-one function. As a result, this function is invertible.

- For graphs I, II, III, some horizontal lines intersect the curve more than once. These are not one-to-one functions. As a result, they are not invertible.

Therefore, the correct answer is "IV only".

knowledge_point.title: Identifying an Invertible Function From Its Graph
